I read the whole file. It has only a few new definitions and they are private: `H2Recon.TG` (a predicate on JZero) and `H2Recon.dispHom` (an additive map from divisors to JZero sending E to the class of g•E − E). The rest is private helper theorems and the final `solution` theorem.

- `H2Recon.TG` is a problem-specific predicate. It says a class has a good representative whose glue datum is a node unit. It is not a Mathlib concept, and I found no existing Mathlib or repo declaration that it duplicates. It could be phrased as membership in an AddSubgroup, but that is a proof-structure point rather than a competing concept.
- `H2Recon.dispHom` is the composite of Pic0.mk with divisor ↦ g•E − E. I checked Def_AlgebraicCurve_BaseChangeGalois.lean for `degZeroSMulHom`, which acts on degree-zero divisors. It is not the same map. Defining `dispHom` through a generic AddMonoidHom would only shorten the proof, and the rubric excludes that.
- `isGoodDiv_add`/`isGoodDiv_addGr` and `glueData_add`/`glueData_addGr` are duplicated theorem pairs inside the file. That is standalone theorem duplication, which the rubric excludes. It is also not a duplicate of a Mathlib concept.
- `ne_zero_of_ord_pos` and `sep_ord_pos` are theorems, so they are excluded as well.

I found no competing definition of a Mathlib concept. I did not check every repo-internal definition exhaustively; the check was limited to the candidates above.
